nodes.name: Solvent-free microwave synthesis of Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB
nodes.procedure: Pt(acac)₂ (10 mg), La(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (7 mg), and KB (5 mg) were mixed and ground in a mortar. The mixture was transferred to a quartz vial and then microwaved for 30 s. After the reaction system cooled down to room temperature, the product was collected by washing and centrifuging with ethanol three times. Finally, product was dried overnight in a 60°C oven.

nodes.name: Solvent-free microwave synthesis of PtLa@CC
nodes.procedure: Carbon cloth (1×2 cm²) was washed and soaked overnight in H₂SO₄:HNO₃ (3:1), and then neutralized with ultrapure water. Pt(acac)₂ (10 mg) and La(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (7 mg) were ground and mixed in a mortar and then evenly coated on the surface of CC. The CC with metallic precursors was transferred to a quartz vial and then microwaved for 90 s. The material was obtained after rinsing with deionized water and ethanol and drying in air at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: Solvent-free microwave synthesis of PtM@KB variants
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of Pt₅₈Gd₄₂@KB, Pt₆₀Tb₄₀@KB, Pt₆₀Er₄₀@KB, Pt₆₀Tm₄₀@KB and Pt₆₂Yb₃₈@KB were similar to Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB: Gd(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (8 mg), Tb(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (8 mg), Er(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (8 mg), Tm(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (8 mg), Yb(NO₃)₃·5H₂O (8 mg) were replaced with La(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (7 mg), respectively. Pt(acac)₂, lanthanide nitrate, and KB (5 mg) were mixed and ground in a mortar. The mixture was transferred to a quartz vial and then microwaved for 30 s. After cooling, product collected by ethanol washing/centrifugation (3x), dried overnight at 60°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines compositions of PtM@KB catalysts (Tables S1 and S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic ratios were determined by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) (Tables S1 and S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows PtM@KB catalysts possess similar sizes and structure to Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These PtM@KB catalysts possess similar sizes and structure by TEM characterization. (Figures S5-S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.24 nm corresponding to Pt(111) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image shows the lattice spacing (0.24 nm) clearly, corresponding to the (111) lattice spacing of Pt (Figure 1b).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing lattice fringes and nanoparticles

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM mapping and line-scanning confirm uniformly dispersed Pt and La elements on KB.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the TEM mapping and line-scanning confirm uniformly dispersed elements of Pt and La on KB (Figure 1c).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM showing nanoparticles with 20 nm scale bar and yellow arrow indicating feature

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis of Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB consistent with ICP-AES results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Figure S4, Supporting Information) analysis of Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB is consistent with ICP-AES.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD and XPS studies prove successful preparation of refractory PtM@KB electrocatalysts (Figures S10 and S11).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, a series of X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) studies were used to analyze these catalysts, further proving the successful preparation of refractory PtM@KB electrocatalysts (Figures S10 and S11, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of both metals in Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB; Pt mainly metallic (60.1%) with oxidized states (39.9%); La shows metallic La⁰ and La³⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S12 (Supporting Information) shows that all two metals are present in Pt₆₁La₃₉@KB. The dominant peaks of Pt 4f₇/₂ and Pt 4f₅/₂ are attributed to Pt⁰ located at 71.36 and 74.69 eV... Based on the relative peak areas, Pt mainly exists in the metallic state (60.1%) with a small amount in the oxidized state (39.9%).
